summary: Latency regression: p95/p99 spikes on continuous batching for dedicated customer (prod us-east)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Parcelly reports sudden p95/p99 latency spikes (up to 3s -> 18s) for text-generation requests served from their Dedicated pool in us-east. Spikes started 2026-02-28 ~09:30 UTC and correlate with periods of increased small-request arrival rates. Suspected interaction with continuous batching heuristics causing oversized batch waits for low-throughput clients.

Impact:
- Customer is experiencing elevated tail latency for production endpoints (affects user-facing product flows).
- Intermittent request timeouts observed (client-side 30s) causing retries and user-visible errors.
- Affects a subset of models on the dedicated pool (redwood-open-3b and redwood-compat-4b).

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (Parcelly-prod-pool) in us-east.
- Serving runtime v2.14.1 with continuous batching enabled.
- Autoscaling enabled; pool size: 4 GPU nodes.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Send steady stream of short prompt requests (mean tokens per request ~40) at 10-20 RPS from a small set of client IPs.
2) Observe p95/p99 on generation endpoint spike during sustained low-burst traffic windows.
3) Disabling client-side retries reduces amplification but does not eliminate spikes.

Observed logs & metrics:
- Traces show queue_wait_time spike preceding long response times.
- Serving logs: repeated entries "batch_wait_threshold_exceeded" during incident windows.
- Scheduler metrics: average batch formation latency increased from ~5ms to ~120ms; occasional peaks >2s.
- No CPU/GPU saturation reported on nodes at time of spikes.

Additional context:
- Customer recently rolled out a client change increasing short-lived sessions (2026-02-26).
- Related tickets: SUP-4821 and SUP-10642 flagged similar p99 continuous-batching issues in hosted environment.
comments: 2026-03-01 Priya Shah (Support): Ticket created after customer alert. Escalated to SRE for immediate triage. Attached sample request IDs and traces from 2026-02-28 09:36 UTC.

2026-03-01 Marco Diaz (SRE): Initial hypothesis: continuous-batching heuristics are waiting for batch fill due to skewed arrival pattern from a small set of clients. Requested scheduler and batch formation logs and a heap of traces. Asked customer for traffic pattern (IP/region sticky).

2026-03-02 James Li (Serving Runtime): Confirmed 'batch_wait_threshold_exceeded' in logs. Not seeing model-level compute stalls. Proposed temporary mitigation: reduce max_batch_wait_ms and disable adaptive waiting for the customer's pool. Will prepare PR for runtime flag and a hotfix config change.

2026-03-02 Priya Shah (Support): Applied temporary config on Parcelly pool: set max_batch_wait_ms=50 and disable adaptive_backoff. Immediate mitigation reduced p99 from ~18s to ~600ms in preliminary tests. Customer monitoring ongoing.

2026-03-03 Parcelly (Customer): Noted reduction in user-facing errors after mitigation but still seeing occasional spikes ~800ms during traffic bursts. Asked for root cause and permanent fix timeline.

2026-03-04 Marco Diaz (SRE): Investigation continues. Scheduling controlled experiment (A/B) to run with new scheduling algorithm from PR #2143 against pool. Linking to github PR for runtime change. Targeting full rollout to dedicated pools by 2026-03-08 if tests pass.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
- Continuous batching waits for fill due to few concurrent clients, causing high batch formation latency -> confirmed by 'batch_wait_threshold_exceeded' logs.
- No evidence of GPU/compute saturation or OOM at time of spikes.
- Scheduler adaptive backoff logic appears to be overestimating expected arrival window for this traffic pattern (short bursts, low concurrency from same IPs).
- Customer's client change (short-lived sessions) increased request inter-arrival variance, exacerbating batching wait.

Data examined:
- Batch formation histograms (pre/post mitigation) show long tail before config change.
- Traces show queue wait dominates end-to-end latency during incidents.
- SRE replayed traffic in staging with same pattern; reproduced p99 spikes when adaptive_backoff enabled.

Next steps:
- Run A/B test of new scheduling heuristic (PR #2143) in staging; measure p95/p99 and tail queue_wait_time.
- Prepare canary rollout to Parcelly's pool with rollback guard and increased tracing.
- Postmortem to capture root cause and long-term mitigations (scheduler tuning, better defaults for dedicated pools, auto-detect pathological traffic patterns and fallback to fixed-window batching).
resolution:
Temporary mitigation: adjusted Parcelly dedicated pool config (max_batch_wait_ms reduced to 50ms, adaptive_backoff disabled) on 2026-03-02 which reduced p99 from ~18s to ~600ms.
Work in progress: runtime change (github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2143) implements improved batching heuristic that avoids long waits for small concurrent client sets. A/B tests scheduled; if successful will rollout to dedicated pools with monitoring and rollback policies.
Follow-ups:
- Run full postmortem and update runbook: 'continuous-batching-investigation' page.
- Add scheduler telemetry alerts for queue_wait_time outliers.
- Consider safer defaults for dedicated pools (lower max_batch_wait_ms) and an auto-detect fallback for skewed client arrival patterns.
